newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast police disperse students with teargas.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast police disperse students with teargas.

text.p: Police in Ivory Coast dispersed student protesters with teargas on Monday when they tried to organise a meeting at Cocody University, the country's biggest campus in the commercial capital Abidjan, witnesses said.

Police sources said several students had been arrested in the incident, which involved several hundred students and followed a weekend meeting between President Henri Konan Bedie and student leaders at his home village of Daoukro.

Months of student protests about grievances ranging from academic and living conditions to demands for unpaid grants, a claim the government refuses to recognise, have disrupted university life in the West African nation.

The government newspaper Fraternite Matin, reporting on Bedie's meeting with the students, quoted him as urging them to return to classes pending a solution. "You will get nothing from me through violence," it quoted him as saying.

Higher education officials say continued disruption could result in the academic year being declared void, a serious prospect for students who would have to wait another year for any chance of obtaining qualifications.
Ivory Coast's universities cater for 60,000 students in buildings designed to house 10,000. Overcrowding is one of their complaints.
